t:
There's a huge library in the Skytower. A thousand years won't be enough to read all of it. However, there's an even bigger library somewhere else. There's a collector among the Great Mages who collects various antiquities. He is willing to pay a high price for a book that he doesn't have.

Of course, I'm talking about Zayan, the author of the Chronicles of Yesteryear, the early elven history. I find this work incredibly boring. It'll take all your willpower to stay awake as you make your way through all these Ekhads Ollatars, Ellekens, Canaans, and Grallons. I've made numerous attempts to finish this bastion of elven wisdom, but I have to concede defeat.

I met Zayan in person. Fergard, Naira, and I took a work of Galenel, Skrakan's apprentice, and went to Nea.

Nea is a small allod. It's famous because this is where Zayan and Skrakan's stasis ritual first worked. The tower was erected in the middle of a valley which used to be deep in mountains. There aren't too many people around.

Most inhabitants work at the Nea tower. Is there much work?

The Nea tower is unusual. It has a very big library with shelves as big as a house.

When I first saw this place with all the books, I had to tilt up my head so high that I got dizzy.

Of course, Zayan doesn't only keep books. He has plenty of artifacts in his collection. He's obsessed with history, so he happily hoards everything he can find.

His apprentices sort through his loot and arrange items according to historical periods. They can't help but argue over every little thing till they're hoarse.

What surprised me most is that elves aren't the only ones who apprentice with him. He also accepts Kanians and even Xadaganians! But that's not all! They never try to cut each other's throats as they argue! There are shouts, but there's never blood.

Apart from the tower, there's an ancient portal system that can take you to different allods. As Zayan defines it, it's a magical crossroads, where many June paths intersect. It's a shame many of the portals don't work.
This is the Guide to Allods by Danas. He tells you true eye-witnessed stories about the allods he visited.

This is the Guide to Allods by Danas. He tells you true eye-witnessed stories about the allods he visited.

It's missing some pages.

It's boring to death. It goes on and on about the modern fashion. Articles about scandals in Great Houses are mildly amusing: "The Great Mage Maximillian's daughter ran away with a stray minstrel!" At the end, there's a horoscope with all Martyrs' Zodiac signs. It predicts love, success, and happiness to everyone.

Some Afanasy Firov's revealing pamphlet about angering Tensess with sins, and how he will take away his Gift soon. According to him, this happened because people turned to demons and started helping them, instead of fighting. Afanasy predicts the end of the world, which will happen soon. It was written just recently.

The report tells in detail how Victoria Korleone was coming to power. Apparently, she lost her parents, and held a grudge, because her brother didn't have enough time for her. Victoria spent many years in orphanage, but then escaped and joined a gang of robbers. Over a few years her cruelty and remarkable intelligence brought her to real power. She used some old connections to restore her father's criminal empire. Her whereabouts remain unknown.

Antoinette de Delice asks Zayan how her daughter Gala is doing, and if she performs well. Antoinette tells about her hardships with representatives of other Great Houses. The lengthy and flirty letter suggests that Antoinette advocates the Elvish neutrality. She has the support of Caspar de Vevre, Florenta's Great Mage, and Baudwan de Grandeur, the Great Mage of Stellar. Renard de Ardeur, the Great Mage of Lumenara, Maximillian de Blizare from Gelida, and Guillaume de Pluie, the Tempesta Great Mage, support Kania. There's a lot of intrigues and fight for power between the Houses.

Great Mage Renard de Ardeur tells Zayan about preparations for the Great Ball. It looks like it's happening soon! According to Renard, the elven society is divided: some of them want to get back to neutrality in Kania/Xadagan conflict. Renard complains that although this isn't a good time for a celebration, they'll have to throw the Great Ball anyway. It can't be delayed. He sends Zayan a warning that vampires of the House de Doucer can't be trusted.

A worn-out contraband sample dated February 1012. There's a half-naked elven girl on the cover. Some of the pages are lost. You flip through the pages and blush. This is a typical erotic magazine with all kinds of elves. None of them is properly dressed. Hide it away!

You read it out loud. It's the only way not to lose track.

"Astral is primal. The source of all being. Pure primal matter. It's creative and destructive. Astral is heterogenous. It's a mirror, reflecting the endlessness. You can see only the first layer, nearest to you. It doesn't mean there's nothing in the depth. It only means you can't see any life deep down. You're a blind fool, who can't see beyond the walking stick. Throw away the stick, and learn to see. Remember. You have a unique opportunity: you can see all Astral mysteries. Step beyond. Nobody knows what awaits you there. One thing I know for sure: if it doesn't kill you, it makes you stronger.
You haven't found this page yet. Try looking in one of the hidden corners of Dale.

It looks like a journal, where some cultists put down orders from his master. It isn't very clear, but it looks like he's talking about the astral demons, who almost ruined the world. Did this cultists worship demons? Crazy fool! Does he want to revive that "Master"?

This letter was written by a Wormface. He reports following Zayan and other elves at the Outpost. The Wormface saw the undead army gathering. He did the headcount of the crowd, which Dakkar loaded onto Eclipse. He continues to watch the Outpost, and wants some of his brothers to follow Eclipse and oversee the battle. Another army is needed on Ammer to infiltrate in some Cosmos-created Desmoterion. The Wormface expresses hope that the Overlord will be pleased by his services.

A recipe of the potion made of ingredients, which are found on different allods: pinecones from Lightwood, forest berries from Lugna, herbs from Forox, and fruit from Florenta. It has a curious effect: it strengthens your spirit and boosts potency.

A late issue, full of mind-bending articles. You don't understand half the words in it. Strange Zem with weird names, such as Semer Palsecam and Yaver Thamphthis are discussing a problem of the so-called "soulless bodies". These poor soulless chaps got into big trouble. The long discussion of "Spark rejection" and "progressive insanity" continues for several pages. You go through the magazine, but there's nothing worthy of attention.

There's a long article called "Jigran: fact or fiction?" It contains Marianna Lopatina's story about exploding rabbits along with certain "expert" opinions, making fun of her. It remains unclear whether the allod Jigran existed or not.

It's a very long interview with a famous elven lady, a private collector of rare antiquities who speculates about the recent events in Sarnaut, analyses prices at the Boutique, discusses latest archeological discoveries and many other things. Too many words, too little sense.

An Imperial-printed cookbook. Nice quality, a lot of colorful images. It offers odd recipes, though. What are "milk sausages" or "aubergine caviar"? What is this?  A certain Yasskul Oliver talks about long-term preservation, and Timur Kefirin goes into these rather long details on marinating barbecue meat. How curious!

This looks like an ancient Kanian cookbook and household manual. "If an unexpected visitor pops in, and you have nothing at hand, welcome them in style with these quick, last minute ideas. Find a pound of butter, two pounds of ham, and a dozen eggs..." This must be a good read. Most of the recipes are uncookable. It's not so easy to find such ingredients as Siverian grouse or Lightwood sturgeon. But you can enjoy the pictures!

A recently printed but hardly legible poster. You can still read the slogans, "Skull's not dead"" and "We are no slaves!" It looks like a call for a riot against the Empire. It would be interesting to find out more, but one leaflet doesn't give you enough information.
A bunch of documents you found in Dale.

A bunch of documents you found in Dale.

It isn't complete.

Skrakan, my friend! I was glad to receive your letter, and I will be more than happy to answer your questions. My people always adored human curiosity.

I'll be brief. The split in the Conclave was inevitable. The changes I mentioned triggered a long discussion on which way to choose.

Alas, not everyone chose the right path. It pains me to admit that some of us no longer belong in here and have to go. I'm speaking about vampires.

I know you have encountered them before. The strange curse you're asking about looks very much like vampirism.

However, I can see the impact of Darkness. The Darkness that, for some reason, prevailed in the June culture in the last years of its existence.

Yes, you are not mistaken. I'm speaking about the mysterious artifact, the Evil Mirror. An amazing creation with a mind of its own. Who knew the consequences could be this devastating?

It wasn't easy to defeat Canaan and his followers.

The betrayal of Elleken and Nemeina was also a blow. I'm afraid our leader is on a dangerous path. He wasn't happy when the Conclave decided not to continue the Transformations... But I should stop here. If dragons aren't perfect, why would we want to be like them?

Sincerely yours, Pascal. The Mebir tower, 2569.

I'm afraid the news are true, my friend!

Tensess has fallen. And it isn't our only loss. We're facing something far worse than the Black Night.

People call it the Night of Astral Portals.

I hear there's trouble on Umoir, too. Is it true? Have Plagot and the Skytower been destroyed? I can't begin to imagine what you're going through, my friend. Fighting off monsters was hard enough: I had to use all reserves and put the stasis spell on pause. As a result, my allod has shrunk.

Luckily, the Tree helps me. I think it can protect the allod against the Astral. But Nezeb is furious. His capital lies in ruins.

This war between us seems wrong, very wrong and untimely. The word is that these... demons appeared on Kirah during the battle between Yasker and Enniel. The elf managed to evacuate his troops on a ship, but our young friend had to leave most of his army behind. I think it's a good thing. Maybe he'll be a little less arrogant.

Now, about our young friends... I hear Catherina arrived at the Kanian Archipelagos after Tensess's death. You know, Smaragd's young apprentice, cheeky and proud member of the Scarge royal family. She has lost her allod. Is she looking to occupy the Kanian capital?

But enough about that. Anyway, I'm writing because I want to know more about the demons. I know that you have encountered one of them a while ago. You know what I'm saying?

These creatures are way more diverse than I could imagine. They literally come in all sizes. It's a shame that most of them ignite and burn spontaneously after death. I'd really like to get a couple of bodies for research.

I hate to think that Nezeb and the one who comes after Tensess will continue the war. The threat before us is way worse and more dangerous than the old feud. I suspect that the demons have some sort of a goal. This is the beginning of a new war. Mark my words! We must understand what we're faced with before we can win.

Your colleague and collaborator, the Great Mage Gorluxor. The Yakhch tower, 910, Allod Age.
You haven't found this page yet. The witches took it. Try looking near the Witch's Lair.

Skrakan, my friend!

I received some disturbing news, so I'm rushing to write you back. I have to tell you that your assumptions are correct. Exploration of other worlds could be dangerous. The Conclave has a very vague idea of what could await us there... I suppose we should consider them hostile...

As far as your folks are concerned, I'm afraid we don't have any other options but to banish the ones that are gripped by this "madness".

You mentioned that they call themselves Rada and Rod now. This is very, very curious.

I sensed an echo of their spells. I must admit, I've never seen anything like it. How thrilling... the magic of life and death...

But all research of this kind must be banned, starting now!

We must destroy all astral tools and come up with a list of dangerous and prohibited literature. I suppose, the Conclave will put the lid on that now and enforce the ban. No one can know what happened!

The same goes for the magic of death and the magic of mind. Raising the dead? Controlling minds? No, this is not how we do it. This knowledge must be available only to the Great Mages under strict control of the Council.

Well, it is decided. I can't wait to meet your new apprentices. I hope you can send them over soon. I'll dispatch one of mine. The young Zayan takes great interest in history. Can you tell him about the foundation of Kania?

Love, your friend Maeve. The Ulrir tower, 2690.

Hello, Skrakan, my dearest friend and teacher!

I hate to tell you this, but I am bringing you bad news. It's Nezeb.

Here at the desert border, I hear reports of what is happening.

Your former apprentice already united the desert tribes. I don't have a single doubt that these nomads will soon invade Kania.

What is even worse, I know that Nezeb is preparing to occupy the territories. His emissary are making promises to the nobility and hire away generals and military officers. As soon as the Ugra army appears at our gates, they're going to let them in.

The Gray Prince plays a crucial role in all this. I wonder what your old apprentice had to do with that.

I have more bad news. I'm sure that the Conclave is about to fall apart. Xos, Lex, Ulf, Rokoit, Irsen, and Gorluxor are in favor of Nezeb.

The future war may become Kania's last unless we take steps to prevent it. The feud will attract orcs. You never know what can happen if the Great Mages begin to fight each other.

Please assuage my fears. Kragg is located at the desert frontier. It will be the first to face the future invasion.

Your loyal apprentice, Yokki. The Yazes tower, 2909.

Glory to you, o Great Skrakan! I beg you to allow your humble servant to deliver a message!

My name is Kakhar, a modest slave of my Emperor, the Sun of the nation, may his name shine forever, may he eternally reign the Xadaganian Empire!

I have learned that Kanian governors are dreaming to get their lands back. I humbly beg you to subdue the madmen! Was the devastation and despair of the last war not enough for them? Are they willing to start over so soon?

The wisdom of the Emperor is higher than the sky, and His servants are loyal and brave. We have established the just laws, bent the heads of the arrogant, and protected the weak in our new land!

The latest deed of the Emperor is unprecedented! Aware of the fact that our lands aren't always clean, He undertook the measures to purge them! He dispatched the Emissary all over the country, to every city and town! They visit every water source and every well, explaining to people how bright their future will be!

We're establishing our country for centuries to come!

I would also like to learn about many mysteries of this world, o Great Skrakan! I beg you, condescend to your humble slave!

If I am allowed to ask: who were the Junes? Where have they gone, and why? I am also very curious about the heritage of the Zem, whose ruins lie in abundance in my motherland. We have many legends that mention that the Zem used to live by a great river and trade with my people. But one day a great disease has come and purged all Zem from the face of the world. I wonder what the reason was.

The legends say about an ancient nation, who lived on ocean islands and could navigate the sea... Our merchants claim that they still come across these people in open sea.

I would very much like to learn all this, o Great Skrakan, but most of all I want to know the history of creation of the Conclave of Great Mages, about the Kingdom of Yrene, and elven mages. The names of Oberon, Pascal, Melusine, and Maeve are familiar to me; I also know a lot about their noble apprentices Zayan, Lorelei, Margo, Gramon, and others.

Alas, the elves today are shielding themselves from the world. They're reluctant to speak to other races, and frontiers of their kingdom are closed and secured.

I humbly hope to hear from you, o Great Skrakan!

Petty servant of the Great Emperor Nezeb, the Great Mage Kakhar. The Imbul tower, 2934.

Skrakan! I'm glad to hear from you.

I agree with everything you wrote. This animosity between Kania and Xadagan has to end. But it won't be easy...

What is the purpose of the Conclave of the Great Mages, after all? Must we enforce the ancient law? Or maybe our goal is bigger than that?

The Conclave split long ago. The elves escaped from the world: I haven't heard from anyone on Yrene for a while. The mages of Kania mind their own business. Plam, Ferr, and Potiphar serve the Valirs. Smagard is busy with his toys. Dean, Marvin, and Aidenus locked themselves in their towers to study spells. Others are... also busy, probably. You know best.

Xadaganians are out of the question. Vodor, Gaphur, and Ulf are Nezeb's minions. Others are more or less independent, especially Yokki and Gorluxor.

We should know better than to waste so much resources on this petty feud. Couldn't we accomplish much more if we united forces? I think we could!

We need a different goal. Wars with orcs, trolls, Lamia, Aviaks, Mountainfolk, and others united Xadaganians and Kanians, but those tribes were never a serious threat.

What could possibly unite us? The search for truth, solving riddles of the universe, wandering along endless roads, trying to find some answers...

We don't know much about the world. How did it come about? Which forces rule it? What is magic?

Zayan has the Key, the Grain of Protopower - this is what I would begin the research with. I know there's a multitude of such keys. There's something in them... Something that must give us the answers.

The time has come to unite the Conclave, Skrakan! All we need to do is end the conflict! Then we can put all our effort into research and discover a lot!

Your true friend, the Great Mage Erast. The Ark tower, 3389.

Skrakan, my friend!

I'm torn with doubts as I'm writing this. Soon we'll be ready for the Grand Experiment.

You know how long it took to prepare... It was a great effort to gather everyone...

But I still have some concerns...

I can't share this with anybody, or they will think I'm insane.

You might not believe me, either. You might think that I dreamed it, that it never really happened.

But it's true.

I have seen the future.

Everything happened so quickly. My apprentices and I were making some final checks and preparations, when suddenly a portal appeared in the room.

This portal took me to an odd world. I was locked in it for some time.

Kania and Xadagan also exist in that world. They're still at odds. But that world is different. It is broken. It's shattered into myriads of allods, floating around in a substance they call "Astral".

Xadagan has done a lot over the past years. A special device enabled time travel. This device was invented by a scientist called Alexander!

Who could've thought that a camel herder can come up with something like that?

He told me they were studying a temporal anomaly not far from Umoir allod. Umoir, Skrakan!

The scientist had no clue why the world had crumbled. Apparently, there are several theories. The world could have been shattered by a meteor. Another one is that the Astral attacked suddenly, like a rising tide.

I have a horrible suspicion... what if our Grand Experiment caused the cataclysm? Or is it because we gave it up, failing to contain the power of the Origins and prevent the death of the world? Who knows...

In any event, we have no choice but to proceed. I used the Key, the Grain of Protopower to enable some stabilizing spells. They're going to help us in case of emergency.

Soon everything will be ready. Good luck to all of us!

Your curious friend, Zayan. The Nea tower, 4015.

Skrakan!

It's a disaster! A complete and absolute failure! We were so foolish...

The world is breaking apart... Something's devouring it... something I can't even name. This substance... cannot be controlled...

The information I receive from everywhere is horrifying.

Mountains are falling. Water in oceans starts to boil. The skies roll up like a scroll.

People are panicking. They run to the cities to be close to our towers, as if looking for our protection.

Many of them are gone. The residual magic recoiled and hit us. Some were less fortunate.

Pascal is irresponsive, and Maeve won't return my calls, either. Someone eye-witnessed the Ulrir tower crumble to pieces and fall.

Zayan thinks there's still hope. Perhaps, we could cast a stabilizing spell, which would contain at least some land mass around our towers.

I don't know what else can be done here. Where do I even start?

I'm afraid, we don't have much time. The world is fading by the hour. The power of the Conclave must be used only to prevent the ultimate death of the world!

Farewell, my friend. I will do everything that I can to save the world.

Your loyal apprentice, Tensess. The Qwator tower, 4015.

Oh, wise Skrakan!

I'm glad to report that my observations have been confirmed. The Astral was stopped, the stasis spell is holding.

We saved the world, but the price was high. I'm afraid the truth about what really happened will ruin us all.

I read your story about Tunure and Imbul... Bloodthirsty mobs... who blamed their Great Mages for what happened and killed them. They also died a terrible death when the Astral consumed their allods.

We have to hide the truth for the greater good.

We'll give them our own version:

"The catastrophe began somewhere in the depths of the universe! It could not be prevented! A huge meteor was coming down! The huge explosion was inevitable. The earth shattered, and the waves of astral poured and destroyed everything in their path. Death triumphed over life. It seemed that there was no hope. We can't begin to describe the despair of those dark days... The last glimmers of hope were consumed by mortal terror - and yet, there was hope! The Great Mages sought a way to stop the doom. They did whatever it took without hesitation. They were strong. Each of them was able to hold a patch of land around their tower. Since then, none of them can leave their allod. Ever!

This is how the new era, the era of allods, began."

We fed this version to the most talented bards. They went to all cities and towns and told our story to everyone who would listen.

We will never forget the names of the heroes who fell while trying to stop the Astral: the twelve Great Mages sacrificed their lives while casting the stasis spell!

The Great Mage Aidenus. Forox allod, the Forox tower, year 12 of the allod era.

Skrakan, my dear friend!

For years, I've tried to understand what you dealt with in the Outer Worlds, and what caused you to seal your allod in frantic haste. One thing is certain - you are alive, and you have encountered a great threat.

Do you remember my magical cape that restores power and health? It helped me in the most desperate situations, especially if a disease was caused by magic. I'm sending it over with my Ambassador.

I gave the Ambassador a scroll with a special spell which allows him to activate the cape even without your help. If the Ambassador finds you, he can cover you with the cape and read the spell. I have no doubt that you will recover your power.

Your friend, Tensess.

Imperial Decree. Schleherloht, summer, year 646 of the allod era. Attention: Danas, Naira, Fergard, Reniesta.

I, the Emperor Valir IV, the ruler of Kania and all of its Allods, blessed by the unparalleled might of the Great Mage Tensess, issue our imperial Decree on this day. By the Decree, an expedition of four subjects must go to Umoir allod on a mission of utmost importance.

The expedition members must make every effort and prove themselves to be true children of the Empire while advancing towards the main goal by all necessary means and carefully studying everything worthy of attention on Umoir.

Commander in Chief's Letter

Admit it, my friends. This is the first private letter you have received from the Commander in Chief. When I handed you this envelope in Schleherloht, I bet you didn't expect to find my instructions in it.

But I'm sure the formal assignment and even the Emperor's decree are less useful than my analysis of the situation. Besides, I'm not sure any official papers can be helpful here.

I hope you will find time to take in the knowledge I'm about to share with you. I'll start from the ancient times.

When you were little, you must have heard legends about Umoir, the allod of the Great Mage Skrakan. How no one has ever returned from there alive. How everyone finds paradise and eternal youth there. And most importantly, legends about unique knowledge and artifacts that grant unbelievable power. I'm sure these are nothing but fairy tales, but essentially, it's something you're supposed to find out yourself.

Umoir is the largest known allod in the world. It was the Great Mage Skrakan who discovered a way to stop the land from crumbling and disappearing. Later, he used this method on Umoir. When the world regained its balance, Skrakan returned to his studies of hypothetical Outer Worlds. We know he was on the verge of an important discovery in the year 576 of the Allod Era. He told this to his friend, the Great Mage Tensess. Tensess waited for more news and tried to get in touch but failed. Umoir appeared to be isolated from the rest of the world. The isolation was caused by a very powerful spell cast from the inside. Any messages, items, or people seemed to pass through the Barrier safely and arrive at the allod. But nothing, absolutely nothing came from the inside.

A lot of expeditions have been sent to Umoir since then. Great Mages and governors sent their best armies and magicians, but no one returned.

Nobody knows for sure what's going on in there.

Even before the war, we dispatched our troops to Umoir. We never stopped trying to solve this riddle. Over the past ten years, 18 Imperial troops of Kania went to Umoir. We know that Xadagan sent twenty. None of them returned or made any contact whatsoever.

Now, to your mission. Despite our great victories, the war has been going on for too long. We're almost out of resources, and so is Xadagan. At this point, only a fundamentally new weapon could grant an advantage to one of the sides. We're conducting extensive research, but espionage and bribery put our effort to naught. We have every reason to think that the Great Mage Skrakan has made a magical breakthrough. Fearing that his discovery could be used to do harm, he isolated himself and the allod. You must find this discovery and find a way to deliver it to Kania. This is your official assignment.

I command you to survive and return, may our land live forever.
This is Skrakan's archive of letters, received from other Great Mages.

This is Skrakan's archive of letters, received from other Great Mages.

It's missing some letters.

Many people treat dark arts with mistrust, and with good reason. Summoners of the old earned an ill name, and of course, the first one that comes to mind is Tep who doomed his people. But there were others, too...

I'm speaking about Urd, the Great Mage of Yazes, also known as the Master of Souls. It happened shortly after Umoir events, when four heroes lifted the veil of mystery and saved Skrakan from the demon.

Yazes belonged to the Xadagan Empire for a long time. But, unlike other Nezeb's provinces, such as Suslanger, Igsh, or Arav, Yazes was somewhat independent. Tensess had to surrender the lands of Yazes to the conquerors after the battle of Molod.

After the world was split into pieces, this allod was preserved by old Yokki, one of Skrakan's apprentices, who joined Nezeb. Yokki was wise enough to maintain balance among the inhabitants of these lands without oppressing any of them. A small druid enclave remained in the Ancient Forest in the west. They were wary of the big city Kragg where noble families of Kania mixed with the chiefs of Ugra tribes and created a new community of Xadaganians.

The arrogant nobles demanded that their rights were respected. This is how they got their own High Knight, King of the allod. The allod dwellers maintained harmony if not peace for a long time, until the Summoner Guild (or, as they were called back then, Necromancer Guild) came to power.
You haven't found this page yet. Try looking near the Witch's Lair.

No one trusts dark mages. No one believed them then either, but they managed to persuade the king to allow them to form their own organization in exchange for an artifact - a crown that protects its owner against the magic of the Astral. It became a guarantee for the king that he will be protected against any possible influence that might come from the guild...

The trouble began when Urd became Yokki's apprentice. After a while, the Great Mage banished his apprentice - and died suddenly a little later. A death of a Great Mage is a rare-case scenario. There were rumors that Yokki's death was set up by Urd.

However, no evidence was found, and Urd became the Keeper of Allod by Nezeb's order. Shortly after that there was an event, known as the Fall of Three Stars. The king has supported the necromants ever since. A lot of bad and evil things happened then. People complained, but nothing could be done.

The arrival of Skrakan's Ambassador was the turning point that triggered an avalanche of events. He was so alarmed by the events that he found it best to send his Emissary to figure things out. Fortunately, Skrakan's Ambassador met a young noble named Iglez. They took part in many adventures together.

Iglez governed one of the villages on Yazes called Lairisha. That was where he and Galenel first ran into Urd's Summoners. Back then, Urd was already gathering an army for an attack on Xadagan, but he still needed recruits for his undead horde. The recruitment process was rough: they took everyone they could, ignoring pleas and protests...

Iglez fought back and won. The village elder gave Iglez a fragment of a Star, an artifact that recently fell out of the sky. That night was known as the Night of Three Stars.

Iglez and Galenel figured that the "star" resembled a fragment of King Yazes's crown.

They wanted to find the other fragments. A local stargazer was the one that could help.

It turned out that the stargazer had been killed by bandits on Summoner Guild's orders. Only his granddaughter Dinah survived.

She used her grandfather's notes to find one of the stars in the Ancient Forest - a mysterious place which was avoided by the locals like the plague. There was a druid settlement in the forest since the times when this land belonged to Kania. They had every reason not to trust anyone from the valley.

Galenel, Iglez, and Dinah had a hard time earning the trust of the druid leader, the great Saken-May, and his associate, the powerful Arafel-Fei. They promised their help in finding the crown fragment.

They found another part in Hemer desert full of wild orcs and goblins. It wasn't easy to make it work, but the brave orc Hinsash helped our friends.

An elf in the Ancient Forest had the third part of the crown.

Some events took place while the company was looking for stars. Tension grew between druids and the Royal Knights, influenced by the Summoners. In the end, Kragg's army moved out to the Ancient Forest. The heroes decided to talk to the king who hadn't been seen for a long while. The King never took off his helmet with closed visor.

It turned out that, when Urd became the Great Mage, he deceived the King, broke the artifact crown into three fragments, and turned him into an obedient zombie. Everyone rose against Urd when it came to light. He was defeated and killed in a bloody battle at the Yazes tower.

Urd's legacy is not as awful as Tep's, but he certainly left a mark.

Heed this warning, one who reads this scroll, and beware - for you are on a dark path.

This is a Summoner's craft - the art of controlling the dead. This knowledge has been forbidden for centuries, so beware of delving into its secrets, because the Conclave's rules are strict, and those who violate them will be severely punished...

What is death? Is this the end - or the beginning of something new?

The answer is unknown. One thing is certain, the spirit of the dead can be summoned. The living can ask the dead their questions.

Summoning isn't all about primitive spiritism. We are capable of much, much more! It is a known fact that dead bodies can rise. This may be caused by a curse - or by some unusual conditions. Brainless creatures crave only warm flesh and blood...

A Summoner is capable of subjugating them. They can even raise the dead from their graves and bend them to his will.

An undead body without a spark is called a cadaver. Depending on its condition, a cadaver can be a skeleton, a zombie, a ghoul, or a walking dead. There is a wide range of different types of cadavers.

It should be clear from the name that the skeleton has no flesh on the bones, while a zombie's flesh is mostly intact. A ghoul is a transformed undead that feeds on other dead and undead bodies.

A true Summoner has mastered the art of raising and handling the undead. They are fully aware of these differences.

We have talked about the undead that have no Sparks, but there are some who do. There is nothing difficult about summoning a Spark and trapping it in an already dead body.

But there is a kind of undead that are not easy to create – ghosts. A ghost is a result of magic – powerful curses that rip the Spark from the afterlife and bind it to a certain place or object...

Ghosts are invulnerable to physical impact, but capable of doing harm or even killing someone.

Ordinary ghosts are the most common type. They are the ghosts that have the same appearance as they had in life. Apart from them, there are banshee, as elves would call them. They're known in Kania as weeping spirits. For reasons unknown to me, only female creatures, especially elven, can transform after death. I carried out a lot of experiments, studied multiple specimen: almost all of them turned to Banshee after death.

Necromants can enclose ghosts in dead bodies, but this requires a great effort. However, the resulting creature can be deadly.

I also know about other cadavers: shape filchers, viys, spark throwers, and others. All of them combine a spiritual component, bestowing them with remarkable intelligence, and a strong undead body, capable of destroying their enemies.

It is time to talk about controlling the undead magic.

A powerful summoner can sustain numerous undead, but there is a question of control. The undead do not take kindly to being disturbed, and it is very difficult to force them to obey...

The Undead would normally hate their Summoner. They kill them the first chance they get.

Do not forget that maintaining life in the undead requires magical powers which tend to expire quickly and abruptly.

It may seem that creation of an undead army is an extremely challenging job, but I think I have found a solution.

I noticed that the willpower is strong enough in some undead to command other undead and even support life in them. The influence is so strong that the undead forget who they were in life and obey their new master.

This is an optimal solution. Instead of giving individual orders to each undead, a Summoner should select the most unruly ones, subdue them, and order them to watch over the others.

This chain can be as long as you need it to be. It all depends on your resources. I chose regular sacrifices to support power in me and my apprentices to maintain our army. The undead of strong will were in control of others.

I hope this knowledge will be useful to all adepts of practical and theoretical summoning.

History has examples for any kind of situation. Unfortunately, sometimes its lessons are too bitter – so we prefer to forget what happened. That's how it went with the events that darkened the existence of elves soon after the Change...

After Junes had perished, there was no kingdom to compare with Yrene in terms of power. Even the last beggar possessed magic powers. The elites of the elven kingdom sought to be even stronger. They immersed into unexplored magic deeper and deeper.

The mysterious magic of June, the blood magic caught their attention. The Junes were desperate and resorted to it more and more, trying to prevent their downfall. But the blood magic didn't help, and the Junes perished. The ancient ruins of their cities are laden with mysterious artifacts, craved by elven researchers.

Some gifts were toxic. The June knowledge significantly boosted the elven necromancy, but also led to some horrible consequences. Some elves used June artifacts to perform bloody magic rituals... and transformed into vampires. Since that day, they were doomed to the eternal thirst, which could be quenched only with hot blood.

Those events are now known as the Blood Feast. The kingdom was divided, so no one felt safe, and each night was full of terror as people expected to be torn apart by monsters who had recently been their friends, colleagues, or even family...

Finally, the vampire hunt began. Even before the events, the kingdom's Council of Mages, headed by the court mage Pascal, gathered a council, henceforth known as the Conclave of Great Mages. It had an important task: to monitor dangerous areas of magic and prevent potential disasters. The Conclave members were horrified to discover that one of them, Canaan, turned into a vampire. They tried to arrest him, but he and his followers managed to escape. The order was restored in the kingdom...

It seemed that Yrene took a fatal blow. The Blood Feast took its toll. The trust among the elves was gone. Many left the kingdom and spread all over larger territories. The elves scattered around the world and began to form Houses, each with their own set of rules and laws.

Some of the vampires escaped their brothers' fate. They hid in the dark. With the June artifacts, such as the notorious Evil Mirror, they were a threat to the world for a long time. Vampire hunters fought an endless war with vampires. Summoning was banned from the elven society for centuries to come. It could only be studied by apprentices who wanted to become Great Mages. It was closely supervised by the Conclave.

The fate of Canaan and his vampire followers has been kept secret for ages.

Still, the vampires appeared here and there, and both humans and elves feared them. The Aro tribes encountered them first...

When vampires appeared, the Aro tribes, ancestors of the Kanians, searched for ways to battle them, but one king went further than others - Vseslav the Sorcerer with his Keepers. They found a way to turn into animals... Wolves, bears, foxes... and other predators.

The problem was, the longer they stayed in their animal form, the more they lost control of their inner beast. One day they got stuck somewhere in the middle.

And now the curse is spread through a bite, just like vampirism. Werebears and werewolves should be distinguished. The former come from intelligent bears. Many wearbears mated with half-bears, half-humans. Today there's human blood in all of them.

The vampire situation improved when human Great Mages took over after the war with orcs. They chased vampires, who span out of control, into the most distant corners of Jule.

They dealt with Canaan himself only in the allod era, when the Vampire Hunters order was created. Their bastion was located in an ancient temple in the mountains.

The Hunters, together with their leader Avelina, followed Canaan for many years. They killed many of his minions, but the final battle took place in the Bastion, when Canaan decided to strike back.

While Avelina was absent, he sneaked into the Bastion and killed everyone inside. The Huntress returned to find the Blood Father standing in the middle of a room among piles of dead bodies.

The legendary battle of Avelina and Canaan was glorified in many songs. Blood Father was struck down by Avelina. His body was taken by the Great Mage Skrakan and buried with great precautions somewhere on Umoir, in a secret coffin.

Galleon Castle. A miracle of engineering created by the House de Ardeur. Many are interested in how this place came to be. Well, it's no great mystery... the mystery is how it turned into the Darkblood Citadel...

Originally, the Galleon Castle was erected by the House de Ardeur. Another Great Ball was prepared back then. It's hard to understand if you know nothing about the Great Game of elven Houses, but the competition between the Houses takes place during every Great Ball. To win, a House must create or show something truly outstanding. Such as a union with Kania, which laid the foundation of the League. Or a technology of astral flights. Or the idea of cultural expansion... Something that could change the world.

It was the House de Ardeur that built the first astral ship - a prototype of League's future first fleet. No wonder that this House has been trying to outdo themselves ever since. This is how the idea of the Galleon Castle came about. It was supposed to turn astral into comfortable environment that would feel like the firm ground of allods.

House de Ardeur moved the construction from their own allod Lumenara to Tenebra, de Desirae residence, out of fear of other Houses' spies. House de Desirae assisted them along the way. They were supposed to receive the Galleon Castle after the Great Ball.

The construction was going smoothly. Both Houses were happy about their own engineering and magical genius. But they didn't expect a treacherous blow from an old enemy.

During the last Great Ball, the House de Desirae gained a victory. Young prince Dakkar ensured it. He was a Summoner. He won the competition against the head of the House de Doucer, Armando. Even though any foul play was forbidden, Armando still took it as a great insult. Once powerful, the House de Doucer had been in decline for half a century after their failed invasion on Kirah. Summoning was Armando's way to regain his former popularity. What a blow it was to be beaten by a boy!

He did what could never be undone. He got involved with Tep. He learned the June blood magic rituals from him and managed to perform the Spark extraction ritual on Dakkar's fiancée, the human girl Svetlana Valir. The young prince tried to lift the curse and reanimate his loved one, but instead, the curse fell on the castle and turned everyone into undead.

Prince Dakkar went into exile. The House de Doucer became a pariah, pursued on every allod. This revenge wasn't good enough for Armando. He tricked Vivien de Ardeur, one of the creators of Galleon Castle. He gave her an artifact, and its power affected and corrupted the whole castle. By that time, the rituals Tep had taught Armando turned Armando and most of the elves in his House into vampires.

Tep wanted to get hold of the technologies that created the Castle. In pursuit of his goal, he needed someone who was involved with the construction. He was lucky to find an ambitious person of low ethics. Armando's wife Camomilla managed to win one of Galleon's creators, Celestine de Ardeur, over to Tep's side. She didn't even have to turn to switch sides! She swore loyalty to the great Summoner just because she wanted to leave a mark in history. Her name was now Nihil. She became an apologist of death and destruction in Tep's service.

Armando was stopped, but the Galleon Castle turned into the Darkblood Citadel forever. It corrupted all visitors with darkness and turned them into vampires. But Raimond and Celestina's brilliant invention didn't go to waste. Armando de Doucer stole the Galleon Castle blueprints for Gorluxor and built a replica. Some time later, after resurrection, Armando used the ship to attack Avilon.

You know what happened next. We defeated them and managed to subdue the ship's mind after a while. The second Galleon Castle has served the Historians well. I hope it will continue to do so.

The House de Doucer wasn't the only family to fall into the trap of vampirism. A similar thing happened to the House de Tristesse. Originally, de Tristesse lived on Umoir, to the east of the market town Al Rihat. Under Skrakan's rule, they traded with humans and did not bother anyone...

Hard times began for the House de Tristesse when Catherina came to power. She banned the trade first, and then banned the House from the allod.

Ademar de Tristesse, the head of the House, had a secret place, where only Kanian hunters could go. It was called Drowsy Woods.

He moved there and took the House and his daughter Annette with him. But it didn't put an end to their troubles. Annette's mother died. Soon, the witch Baba Yaga seduced Ademar, married him, and became Annette's step-mother. She deeply hated her step-daughter. Yaga was jealous, cruel, and so full of herself! Annette was bullied and humiliated. The new wife bossed Ademar around and kept the House on the toes.

But that’s not all. Ademar once brought a hand mirror from his travels. Not an ordinary mirror. It was the notorious Evil Mirror that destroyed Canaan.

Yaga asked the mirror, who was the fairest, and the mirror replied, Annette! The witch got mad and decided to destroy her. Annette ran for her life into the forest, where seven knights lived.

But the witch found her even there... The heroes went out to hunt, and when they returned, she was there, beautiful, pale, not moving or breathing... with an apple in her hand. They guessed that it was Baba Yaga that poisoned the poor thing. They put her in a crystal coffin and left it out there on a high mountain.

Her fiancé Yelisseus killed the witch and broke the crystal coffin.

The witch had cursed Annette. The power of the mirror turned her into a vampire, and the curse took her body and soul. Yelisseus stayed. He hoped he could fight the curse, but he couldn't!

Everyone, who was there with her on the allod, turned into ghouls, just like she was. This is how the House de Tristesse came to worship and protect the Evil Mirror. Some managed to escape, but Drowsy Woods turned into a death trap that no one could approach.

The Great Skrakan is wise and clever. He ruled over Umoir since ancient times, and he was a reasonable and fair ruler.

The world was divided between two states, two Empires: Kania and Xadagan, ruled by Skrakan's apprentices, but the Great Mage himself kept out of their conflicts...

Skrakan was the head of the Conclave. Magic and world mysteries were his major interests. But his main interest lied in Outer worlds. Skrakan wanted to know how to get there.

He tried to solve this mystery for a long time. He was aware that ever since ancient times the Great Mages tried to observe the stars. They thought that stars were other worlds - perhaps, even inhabited! They were looking for ways to send a message out there, to the stars. The luckiest of them received a reply from out there. The reply was rather sad: an unidentified force from space possessed and controlled the brave mages.

The Conclave issued a decree, prohibiting the stargazing for mages. The possessed mages were banished. Some of them escaped to the edge of the world and became local gods of wild tribes.

Skrakan was aware of the danger, but he also thought that there could be someone else that he could talk to and listen to their advice. There was only one thing that Skrakan craved for: he wanted to reverse the world fracture.

Alas, his task was more complicated. Since the astral almost consumed the world, the inhabitants couldn't see the real stars, the sun, and the moon. What they saw were illusions created by the Great Mages.

The astral shrouded the stars and other worlds, isolating them from Sarnaut.

Everyone knows the story of how Skrakan summoned a Demon.

Umoir was under a seal of secrecy for seventy years before the Great Mage was rescued.

Skrakan repented his mistake. However, he continued his research, but he was more careful now. He wanted to know more about the likes of this Demon. In another thirty years he noticed a strange astral wizardry on a different allod, Yazes.

All his Ambassadors were busy at that time. He had to find a volunteer in Plagot. Just one witch replied. Galenel, young yet ambitious. Skrakan sent her over to Yazes.

It turned out, that the source of the astral magic were the spells cast by Urd, the Great Mage of Yazes, who practiced necromancy. It wasn't easy to defeat them, but Galenel and some local heroes could do it. And Galenel delivered Urd's records and artifacts to Skrakan.

The Great Mage started thinking. He didn't want to keep the dark items in the Skytower. Leaving them unprotected was even worse.

Then Skrakan chose a small town of Veligrad that lied at the Clear Valley to the north of Plagot and ordered to build a tower. He moved his apprentice Galenel in there. Her task was to study the legacy of Urd and some other dark mages.

Skrakan then turned back to studying the spell that opened way for the Demon.

Over time, Veligrad grew large and prosperous, while its residents looked warily at the sorceress's tower near the city. They knew dark secrets were kept there.

Sorcerers and sorceresses, Galenel's apprentices, visited the city and spread rumors. They said Urd himself was buried somewhere near the tower, and that there were catacombs under the city - with graves where Skrakan and Galenel hid their secrets.

Skrakan made an interesting discovery. He found that an alien force entered this world very long ago. That was the time when the June people died. What a mysterious coincidence.

He reached out for Zayan, the Historian and requested information about the Junes to study their legacy. Over time, Zayan confessed that all this time he was in touch with the last June. There was a portal to Gipat on Zayan's allod Nea. The last June Tka-Rik lived in cellars of Gipat.

Tka-Rik couldn't tell Skrakan everything, but he warned him time and again about the dangers of the outer world and their living beings.

All was well, but then another trouble arrived. The Orcs, Goblins, and Cyclops lived on Umoir since ancient times... Their numbers changed from year to year; they usually lived in forests, sometimes robbing travelers, even though guards kept them mostly in check.

And a giant named Leviathan gathered them and formed a horde which rampaged through the allod.

At that time, the League was already founded, the secret of astral ships discovered, and the League was gathering forces to attack the Imperial allods.

Nobody knew that Umoir was in danger. They couldn't fight back against Leviathan at first. There were fire and swords of his armies. Many towns were plundered.

Al Rihat was among the plundered towns. They didn't spare Veligrad that lied halfway on the route from Plagot to Al Rihat, either.

The city stood for a long time. Defenders fought like lions, supported by the mages from the tower. But eventually, Veligrad fell under Leviathan's onslaught. The long stand angered the enemy. They spared no one. Everyone was killed.

But they were avenged! Shortly after that, Skrakan gathered an army and the reinforcements from other allods. They defeated Leviathan and got so enraged, they killed every orc and goblin they could find on the allod. The enemy army was completely defeated.

The tower held many valuables when it fell. The Scroll of Tensess was among them - the one that freed Skrakan. And Tensess's coat as well.

Everything was stolen by marauders. Then witches came to the ruins. Before, they watched the tower's treasures with envy, but now that it was unprotected, they rushed to get their hands on the valuables...

They managed to steal a thing or two before, but this was a real feast for the scavengers. Many of these things are now lost forever. Among the things that were lost was the Great Mage's archive, along with his journals.

At first, Skrakan was going to restore Veligrad. But the new war between the League and the Empire was starting at that time. The taxes were spent on rebuilding the fleet and reequipping the army.

What's more, Skrakan moved to Kanian Archipelagos to replace Tensess. Catherina became the new queen of Umoir.

That happened after the Black Night when the demon attacked. Plagot, the capital, was one of their targets. Those were the times of hardship for Umoir. Disasters came one after another.

Catherina wanted to have it her own way. She built Hightown up above, and her tower over it, instead of Plagot. She decided not to restore the old towns, paying closer attention to shipyards and engineering schools.

Little by little, Dale fell into decay. People lived here in small villages, but they were wary of the ancient ruins. And they had every reason to!

The people of Clear Valley have always been Old Believers. They were partially influenced by the Guardian Ring that watched the woods and erected idols of the Sage, Warrior, Hunter, Master, and Maiden.

The new Queen did not like that. And if the first years of her rule were spent developing technomagic, building shipyards, smithies, and schools, over time she decided to lead everyone to the Light...

At first, it was voluntary: whoever wanted, could go to the Church, others were free to visit the local altar. After a while Catherina starting losing her temper.

Those were the times when League decided to elect kings of allods. Many people liked Catherina back then, both common people and the nobility.

But after she became the queen and the Great Mage of the allod and seized all power, the first thing she did was to level the altars, arrest wizards and witches, and introduce taxes for those who ignore the Church.

The were people, who obeyed vigorously. All sorts of inquisitors and templars have arrived. Many of them came from Forox, where the Church gained considerable influence and power. Nadezhda Sialova, a true and very cruel fanatic, became Catherina's deputy on Umoir.

People didn't like it. In particular, the nobility resented her the most. A riot began, but it was too late. They got arrested. Some were executed, others were sent to mines.

Life was never easy in the Clear Valley, but now it turned into a real nightmare. On top of that, the undead were noticed in the ruins. Ghosts, at first. But then came ghouls, banshee, and zombie, as if something has awakened them.

And lastly, the Blight began. It spared no one in other lands, but it was particularly bad in the Valley. Huge mushrooms began to grow, and animals turned into monsters. A Clear Valley turned into a Foul Dale! People tried to run, but it couldn't happen. The undead from the ruins attacked settlements. Only some of them could survive. And this is how the Dale was until some heroes arrived and started fighting the Blight.

We'll begin our story.

The Kanian nation is old, and no one knows where it originates. It is only known that, when Yul still existed, they lived in the northern forests and swamps full of game. Some nations kept away, because few knew the way through the deadly marshes.

The Aro - that's what the Kanians called themselves at the dawn of time - were a brave and strong nation. But other powers ruled the world then. Powerful Junes built their empire to the south of their territories. In the west, the Aro lands bordered the elven kingdom. The east with its boundless steppes was occupied by ruthless orcs.

None of them encroached on the Aro... Except the dragons, fire-breathing serpents that warred against all other nations. They attacked the ancestors of the Kanians as well. That was the era of legendary knights and warriors that fought to defend their homeland. But they were no match for the dragons, and only the forests protected them against complete extermination.

Everything changed when the Junes eliminated almost all dragons. The Aro tribes grew, and soon their forests and swamps were too small for their numbers. And then trackers and merchants brought news: the June people were no more. They vanished as though they had never existed. Only ruins of their cities and fortresses remained. So the Aro started moving to the south...

Oh, the beautiful and bright Kanian land! You astonish with your beauty: numerous lakes, deep rivers, steep mountains, high hills, vast forests, lovely fields, various animals and birds, great cities, lovely villages, noble masters, respectable lords and ladies – you offer so much, Kanian land...!

The Aro came here from distant lands, from beyond forests and swamps. There were so many of them! Leaders and kinds guided them. They spoke many languages, and sometimes failed to understand one another, although their languages sounded so much alike!

The Aro people had numerous enemies: vampires and ghouls, forestfolk and spiritwoods, trolls and ogres.

The worst among them were the orcs.

Nasty folks came from the steppe and occupied the empty towns of June people. People say, orcs used to live in the steppe by the White sea. When Junes and dragons started taking them down, one of the tribes moved across the sea, through storms and hardships, to the faraway land named Isa. That was the Northern tribe. They enjoyed living their lives full of robbery and crimes for a while, but then the local folk kicked them out.

The Northern tribe came back and found that other orcs grew in numbers while they were gone. There were no more Junes or dragons, so the orcs bred themselves into a worldwide infestation.

And the great leader came out of the Northern tribe, united the orcs, and called the big tribe the Horde.

That was a time of great sorrow. When the Horde came, many cities fell, many nations and tribes disappeared, and so worry and fear spread among the people of Aro. It was difficult to watch us. And our joy turned to sorrow. In all towns and villages, people wept and wept aloud.

The same year, the orcs took the capital, the great city of Dreslavl. They killed the people and burned the city. They captured many prisoners and took loot, and then returned to their camps. There was a great dismay. People didn't know where to run.

The Aro tribes weren't united. Each had their own king. However brave they were, they couldn't confront the Horde power. And the orcs spread, like a river during the flood. Nothing could stand in their way.

Many people were captured: seasoned men, beautiful women, wise old men, and little kids. The orcs made some of them slaves. Others were killed and eaten.

All hope was lost, but suddenly, there was deliverance!

There was a sage, who travelled a lot around the world, looking for apprentices. He stood up and fought against the orcs. His name was Skrakan.

He gathered all kings together in Ar-Kania on a summer day and gave a long speech. He said, everyone will perish unless an alliance is formed. Skrakan's apprentices Tensess and Nezeb agreed on that.

Valir, one of the kings stepped forward, and vowed not to lower his sword until the last orc is expelled from the lands. Other kings made the vow. This day is known in history as the Unity Day. The Aro tribes became Kanians.

It took a great effort to defeat the orcs. Many feats were accomplished, and many glorious battles were fought.

At the beginning, kings and sorcerers gathered an army and defeated the orcs that plundered the land, and they were led by Skulnar's son - the cursed Stormrider the Northwind.

Valir defeated Stormrider. And that was how the resistance began.

The Horde is here today, gone tomorrow with the loot. Skullnar, the orcish leader, was smart. He knew immediately that the people had the power now. He avoided the last battle as hard as he could, but the raids continued.

Skrakan erected strongholds in Horde's path. He built outposts and prisons. His best friends Tensess and Nezeb used their magic vision to spy on the Horde tribes and see where they were going.

This is how it was now. Valir and the troops patrolled the roads, saving prisoners and returning people's possessions. The strongholds and outposts didn't let the big orcish army pass.

While saving prisoners and captives, Valir noticed a girl, beautiful like sunrise. Her name was Swan. But he wasn't the only one. Thunder, Skulnar's younger son, wanted Swan, too - as a slave or for dinner, as an exquisite dish.

They got married, and soon Swan gave birth to a child. They named their son Qwator. Later on he founded the city. And now, this city is the new capital.

When old Skulnar heard the news, he became so angry he slaughtered all his servants and howled like wolf, because he had only one son left. Skulnar decided to gather a new army that would be more terrifying than the Horde... He summoned many tribes to join him: trolls, ogres, cyclops, and even goblins.

Then the best and loyal friends, Tensess and Nezeb, had an unusual idea. The two of them rode their horses to the steppe.

Nobody knows how they managed, but they defeated all enemies on their way, and reached the orcish camp. They had to sneak and crawl, but finally, they got to Skulnar's tent.

They entered, hacking and slashing enemies with lightning bolts and fire arrows. And the old chief stepped forward. He took out his sword and wanted to kill Tensess, but Nezeb covered his best friend... and received a wound. Together, they defeated Skulnar the Chief, took his dead body to the steppe, and buried.

The other orcs knew nothing of it. They came in the morning to discover a heap of dead bodies. They started to fight and blame one another. There was a great discord among them. Hailstorm, Skulnar's last son fled far away into the steppe when he saw it.

Tensess and Nezeb returned safely. They didn't tell anyone what happened, but from now on, the orcs were no longer a threat to Kania.

The war with the orcs was over, and Kanian cities grew even more prosperous. They had other enemies to deal with - Lamias, Mantes, and on occasion, a completely different foe.

Back then, elves were divided - their mages fought among themselves for some reason. So the Conclave had empty seats - and the elves admitted the Skrakan first, and then Tensess with Nezeb...

The Conclave made sure that no one engaged in forbidden magic. The violators were punished.

Young Valir, the grandson of Valir, the son of Qwator was the great King. Despite he was called a king, the real power belonged to Tensess and Nezeb. Tensess was a calm person, always willing to listen to others. Nezeb, on the other hand, was hotheaded and short-tempered. They reinforced and complemented each other for a long time...

But Kania grew. New lands were added every year. And finally, it grew almost as large as the June Empire in its highest state. In the south, it was bordered by a hot desert. In the north and west, the country overlooked the Great Ocean. There were vast steppes in the east.

Valir, Qwator's son loved children and gave life to many of them. He found a place for every child in his empire. He sent all of them to rule a kingdom of their own. Over time, Valir's descendants mixed up with the princes, and that's how the modern nobility came to be.

Being princes wasn't enough for them. Some of them referred to themselves as kings, and Valir, the son of Qwator, declared himself the Emperor in the twilight of his years.

Tensess looked at this condescendingly. The real power was in the hands of Nezeb and himself. Nezeb found the argument among Valir's grandchildren more and more disturbing by the year. Sometimes it wasn't just words. Weapons were drawn.

Nezeb would have put up with it, but there were those who wanted to turn them against each other. Gray Prince was the worst. He had a network of spies and assassins for his gray needs.

One day they had a bad fight, and although Tensess and Nezeb used to be best friends, on the following they challenged each other to a magical duel. But this is a different story...
This is a book that follows the history of the Kanian ruling dynasty, its origins, foundation of Kania, and the appearance of Kanian nobility.

This is a book that follows the history of the Kanian ruling dynasty, its origins, foundation of Kania, and the appearance of Kanian nobility.

It's missing some pages.
Wow, what landscapes I have already managed to draw…
Did she tell you using it could tear your arm off? Fine, here.

Yeah right! You are flying to an island full of angry draconids, who are even angrier when you intrude in their home! That’s a far more serious risk of losing an arm, leg or your head than some sixty percent chance that one of you loses your arms using the teleporter. Take it and go.
Ah, , glad to be back in Umoir? This is where this long story began and, apparently, this is where it will end.

Silly keys... I wonder what made Nihaz create them. Alas, I know little more than you do about them. Perhaps Zayan can tell us more? If you're interested, ask him.

I don’t have time for pointless discussions. Anyway, ! Before we had to run head first into two stubborn gods, we already had two keys. The first Key was on Ferris, in that crazy Jeeg’s laboratories. You stole the second key from the wormfaces’ Temple. Both Keys were annihilated after the explosion...

They can be restored. How? I have no idea. However, you already had a chance to take part in restoring a Key. Yeah. Remember Twilight Isle, the fight with Ar’Kanim, his blood mixed with the wormface’s blood? Yes, yes, the dragons got their key then, which Lickflame was supposed to use to open the Star Gates. But who had the chance to stop him? You did!

And what happened to that key? Soliskar and Agrus took it. And only after you managed to find the dragon hunter Harat’s diary did I understand where it could be hidden. On that very island – on Heart of Fire.

I’d like to think we can just teleport there... And that’s exactly what we’re going to do! At first the problem was pretty obvious: no matter how strong I am, I just don't know where to teleport us, but then Gala came to my aid.

The House de Delice is famous for its portal magic, but also for the number of lovers had by its leader, Antoinette de Delice!

So Gala promised that her experimental teleporter would let me teleport right to the draconids own teleporter. I don’t know how exactly this works, but it’s our only chance.

Do you realize HOW MANY draconids are on that island? We don't need another war. Our only chance is to quietly snatch the key! And quickly move it to Eclipse. After all the delays at the beginning, local intrigues and showdowns with vampires and goblins… Let’s just say we don’t have much time left. Go see Gala now. Actually... If you want to learn more about the Keys, I think you should talk to Zayan.
Idiots... why did you come here?

I was sent to investigate... We had to be sure...

There... so many now... so many... they are ready... ready...

Ready... to strike! Wipe away everything! Everything!

Agrus is possessed by hatred... He wants to erase the doomed world... And us with it...

They have been secretly gathering strength for several years now... This isn’t the only island... There are thousands... thousands!

Draconids breed at a terrifying rate... The world knew nothing of them until very recently. And in just a few years they have multiplied so intensely they threaten to overwhelm the whole world and wipe away everything in an avalanche of scaly flesh...

And now there is no one to stop them... The Destroyer Temple is ruined... They are dead... by your hand!

And my people... have committed a grave crime...

They... swore allegiance to the Dark One...  that’s how they want evade death... in a doomed world... that will soon be swallowed in darkness!

Many were against it... but now power is held by those... who forgot... Nihaz’s betrayal...

Now they have accepted the darkness... and they serve it...

Now... let me peacefully... die...
It’s hard enough controlling everything by myself around here...

Zayan is a longtime friend. Moreover, if you remember, my house used to live here – on Umoir. I know this allod well.

I gave the reins of leadership over to my Counselor – Rosie de Tristesse, who will now rule what is left of the House de Tristesse in the Patriarch’s Residence. Now I am free and ready to help. Of course, I am no necromancer... but no one will refuse good advice.

And I am also here, .

The time has come to leave Avilon.

Zayan needs me as a vampire specialist. Perhaps you have already met some members of my family? Yes, the last rebellious vampires were relevant here.

So, I may prove useful.
My dear friend! I have not forgotten your help.
Someday we will give Veligrad a worthy renovation. Or rebuild it.
There’s no time to think about morals right now. Our entire world is at stake.
I can't even imagine how you must feel. Anyway, after everything you've seen in your life... You’ll cope with this too. But we need to move on. Let me know when you are ready.

Then listen up. Things didn’t work out with the vampires, but we've already come a long way with our army of undead. Let's go even further. Ordinary zombies are good, but there are more powerful creatures. Ethereal, nearly invulnerable and very dangerous. Ghosts.

However, they have certain challenges. In most cases, ghosts are magical beings created by complex spells, when the Spark of a creature that was recently alive is somehow bent to the will of a necromancer...

I’m not Tep, and I don’t intend to harvest from the living by stealing their Sparks...

But luckily, we know a place with a lot of ghosts. They are essentially ownerless. I’m talking about the Show on Gipat.

Delmon told me that you conducted certain... investigations there. You found out that Nihaz was behind all this. He used the Light magic to enslave their will, entangling and pulling them like a puppeteer manipulating miserable marionettes.

I think this is a good chance now to hit his weak spot. For some reason, Gipat is very valuable to him. After all, he did bear the name Gorislav Gipatsky...

You and Dakkar can gain control of these ghosts for us. And the second part of Urd’s journal that you found will help.
You can take rest, but every day counts. Go.
Father’s a monster. Mother’s also a monster. Oh well, such is life.
Yes, but I‘m not a mind reader. So, tell me everything in order.

There isn’t much to say – now you're a vampire, congratulations. The strange thing is how quickly it came on... We have no cure for it, as you know, so I can only advise you to strive to remain human.  However, I can tell you a couple important things.

First – the thirst is intolerable.

Second – the thirst is not constant.

You can suppress it with the blood of animals or people. Animals are the best option, or humans who are your enemies, but be careful – if you drink the blood of the innocent, it will taint your Spark. I won’t even mention the consequences if someone notices you doing that...

Third – being a vampire has its pluses.

When you are full, you won’t just feel better, you will also possess certain... Special abilities. When you became a vampire, you acquired two natural vampire skills:  blood feast and transforming into a bat! But remember – a hungry vampire  won't manage such a difficult transformation...

Please. Have fun. Your vampirism complicates our situation a bit, but that’s no reason to give up. Now go and practice your skills. Luckily, unicorns live nearby. When you've had enough – return to me.
Hurry up, we don't have much time.
I don’t remember my own name and don't even know how many years I’ve been sitting in one place... Ask the others. Maybe someone kept their sense around here.
Wow, you're not one of us! But who are you?
Freedom? Freedom?? We've been walking in circles here for many years now, every day the same... If only we knew how to break this circle?!
Who are you? Your face is familiar, but what is your name?

The Chosen, the Chosen has come! Did you hear, woman?

The will of the one who imprisons us here is stronger than a chain of meteorite steel. Understand, oh “great” Chosen?
I think I remember you. Are you the Chosen?

Liberator! You have come...

…

Oh no! Run! The Master is near! He will return us to his box of darkness, tears and hopelessness! Run, save yourself, he is here!
Who are you, wanderer? What do you want?

Yesterday was the same. Today is the same. Tomorrow will be the same.

I know nothing else. Once we were... free?

Now there is only one will over us. His will.

Yesterday was the same. Today is the same...
Could something be different today? I don't remember meeting you yesterday...

There is no deliverance for those who live in a prison world. Don’t you get that?

Each lost soul is in the keeper’s power. There is NO WAY OUT.
Have you heard? They're weeping, they're moaning, they're suffering! Do you hear that?
The Show Stele is guarded by me and maintains the integrity of the Show. Only the one who defeats me may approach it. The weak shall perish. I don't care about anything else.
Oh, the trials life throws at us!

I understand you still have little experience controlling the dead, but it’s quite simple –  they will unquestioningly obey any order you give them.

Remember two things: they are already dead and the “life” in them is sustained through your life. That means all damage they take is redirected to you. But that also works in the reverse:  what gives them strength, also fortifies you. I doubt you’ll be able to even lift a weapon – all your concentration will go towards maneuvering the troops.

I’ll give you the best, use their powers wisely. Well, are you ready to do what must be done?
I didn't expect any other answer.

There is little time, so listen to everything right now...

We will throw our main forces into fighting the Templars on the bridge and outside the walls of the Outpost. We can’t let them take it, but some troops will probably get in!

You stay here. Urd's knowledge allows me to give you a squad of undead that will be strong enough for your mind and soul.  Try to take care of them.

How can you be happy about that?! Those bloodsucking beasts are worse than Nihaz’s demons. They can only lie and betray! Hiero was supposed to deal with this problem, but even he succumbed to darkness!
I don't care, . Do what you must.

House De Doucer. You think they are worthy of redemption? But I... I hate them! Armando killed my father... He killed everyone I knew, except Dakkar. I spent twenty long years as an undead, flying around in a coffin! Armando got off too easy for what he did to me! I want them to suffer as I have suffered!

I am Svetlana Valir, a princess and the rightful heir of my ancestors. Kania is mine by right! And I will take revenge on my enemies! If you think I’ll deny everything... you are mistaken!

Yes, I did that. I am also behind the conspiracy of the nobles! I managed to sic them on the vampires and break that alliance...
What a terrible siege, ... So many dead...
Yes it is... Are you sure you want to be rid of it?
Oh, well great! We’ll save some antidote...
Don't distract me unless there is something important.

Yes, that’s all true, and I don’t like it any more than you do. But Zayan is right about one thing – this is a far lesser evil than Nihaz’s victory would be. I don’t enjoy discussing these things. If you like – talk to Zayan about it. But now you need to go to Annette. She is waiting for you by the eastern entrance.

I’m afraid not. I proposed that idea to Zayan, but he forbids it. Annette is too strong, and if that is obvious to us, then to the vampires... She is the only one who can win their loyalty and command them.

Great news. That means we truly have done all we can.

You know, it was almost easy. I thought it would be harder. It seems Nihaz is waiting for us to make the first move. Well. We won’t disappoint him!

Cosmos has already arrived here on Umoir. He wants to be sure everything is in order. Go and report to him that the army is ready.
The old man disappeared and left a chest behind... Now it seems entirely ordinary and you can’t understand how all those things fit inside it.

And how am I different from the others? Another subdued soul, another leader of your ridiculous army...

Reniesta... how am I remembered? As a traitor who betrayed her friends. I wish none of this had happened. Minute break...

You see, Weglud and I were once quite close. Then he disappeared for many years. As it turns out, he was living in Al Rihat. He was searching for a way to enter the Skytower, and also wanted to get his hands on Tensess's artifacts...

I betrayed myself most of all by joining his side. We were the “Umoir Four” and now everyone only remembers Danas, Naira and Skrakan... My own fault, but now even in death I will do everything to redeem myself.

I can't say your goals are wrong, but your methods... I don’t know. I’ll have to help you now that I see what is happening... But neither you nor Dakkar are forgiven. Actually, there is something else...

When Dakkar performed the ritual, I tried to hide... In your body. And I saw in there... Well, I’m impressed that even the curse of vampirism hasn't shaken your resolve.

No matter how against what you’re doing I am, I can't stop you...

Hmm.

Touching the Soul Shard of another Great Mage had a noticeable effect on me.

At some point, our minds were one... I saw much of what Urd saw, felt his emotions, passions, and desires...

Oh, Urd was very ambitious. Yokka never understood who his pupil really was. He secretly studied forbidden works, traveled across the Hemer Desert looking for Tep’s diaries... Then he murdered his teacher in cold blood.

Sure, we needed Tep here too, but Urd had different plans – he did not seek personal immortality at the cost of many lives, he planned to create his own Empire by overthrowing Nezeb.

An empire of necromancers! What do you think of that?

Anyway, I feel he has gotten stronger. Urd unintentionally passed his memory and power to me. Now I just need to use them for good.

Our strength grows each minute. We have summoned every corpse we could from Veligrad and its surroundings.

But it's too early to celebrate victory. Veligrad’s resources are cleaned out, and our army is only half as big as it should be. Fortunately, there are still many places where we can get new warriors.

Are you interested in our ghouls? The ghouls are all ready.

This type of undead are natural necrophages, that is – corpse eaters. We use them, among other things, to clean up unfortunate zombies. Of course, they need to be kept separate from the rest. Without supervision they will seriously shrink our army.

As for the pirate – my conversation with him was very interesting. Ah, the pirate’s life – lost islands full of treasure. Our friend sent me approximate coordinates. Maybe when this is all over, I’ll organize an expedition.
